svg.title: Three decades of large earthquakes trace the Ring of Fire
svg.desc: Geographic hexbin map of the world. The globe is tiled with regular hexagons; each is shaded by the number of magnitude-5.5-and-above earthquakes that fell inside it, from 9,000 events in all. The warm ramp runs from pale straw (one or two quakes) through orange to deep red (the busiest cell, 218 quakes). The red cells draw a near-continuous horseshoe around the Pacific — the Ring of Fire — from the Andes up through Alaska and the Aleutians, down past Japan, the Philippines and Indonesia to Tonga, with a second belt along the Himalaya and the Mediterranean. Continental interiors and the deep ocean stay almost empty. Equal-area Equal Earth projection.
svg.text: The Earth’s earthquakes draw a Ring of Fire
Large quakes (magnitude 5.5+) binned into hexagons · the deep-red cells trace the Pacific rim’s subduction zones
216 hexagons hold quakes · the busiest holds 218, all on the Pacific rim
One hexagon ≈ 250,000 km² · colour = earthquake count per hexagon · illustrative catalogue seeded on real subduction arcs · Equal Earth (equal-area) projection
